entries.sanskrit:
उक्तश् चतुर्भिर् अध्यायैः क्षत्तुर् मैत्रेय-सङ्गमः ।

संवादस् तु तयोः स्कन्ध- द्वयेनाथ निगद्यते ॥

द्यु-नद्या गङ्गाया द्वारि हरिद्वारे आसीनं न तु कर्म-व्यग्रम् । तत्र हेतुः---अगाधोऽपरिच्छिन्नो बोधो यस्येति । मैत्रेयस्य सौशील्यम् आर्जवादि, गुणाश् च करुणादयस् तैर् अभितृप्तः । पाठान्तरे क्षत्तुः सौशील्यादिभिर् अभितृप्तं सन्तुष्टं मैत्रेयम् ॥२॥
word_for_word: uktaś caturbhir adhyāyaiḥ kṣattur maitreya-saṅgamaḥ
The meeting of Vidura with Maitreya was stated in four chapters.
saṃvādas tu tayoḥ skandha- dvayenātha nigadyate
The dialogue of the two is described in two cantos.
dyu-nadyā gaṅgāyā dvāri haridvāre āsīnaṃ na tu karma-vyagram
He was seated at Haridvāra, at the door of the celestial Ganges, not occupied with worldly work.
tatra hetuḥ---agādho’paricchinno bodho yasyeti
The reason is that his knowledge is unfathomable and boundless.
maitreyasya sauśīlyam ārjavādi, guṇāś ca karuṇādayas tair abhitṛptaḥ
Maitreya’s gentleness, straightforwardness and other qualities, together with compassion and the rest, satisfied him.
pāṭhāntare kṣattuḥ sauśīlyādibhir abhitṛptaṃ santuṣṭaṃ maitreyam
With another reading, Maitreya was satisfied by Vidura’s gentleness and the like.
entries.literal_english: The meeting of Vidura with Maitreya was stated in four chapters. The dialogue of the two is described in two cantos. He was seated at Haridvāra, at the door of the celestial Ganges, not occupied with worldly work. The reason is that his knowledge is unfathomable and boundless. Maitreya’s gentleness, straightforwardness and other qualities, together with compassion and the rest, satisfied him. With another reading, Maitreya was satisfied by Vidura’s gentleness and the like.

entries.sanskrit: प्रश्नान् एवाह---सुखायेति पञ्च-दशभिः । तैः कर्मभिः । सुखं वान्यस्य सुःखस्योपशमं वेत्य् अर्थः । अथवान्यद् वा न विन्देत । किं तत् ? इत्य् अपेक्षायां तस्यैव निर्देशः । उपारमं वेति । ततस् तैः कर्मभिर् भूयः पुनः पुनर् दुःखम् एव विन्देत । अत्रैवं विधे संसारे नोऽस्माकं यद् युक्तं कर्तुं योग्यं तत्-सर्व-ज्ञो भगवान् वदेन् निरूपयतु ॥२॥
word_for_word: praśnān evāha---sukhāyeti pañca-daśabhiḥ
He now asks the questions, beginning with “for happiness,” in fifteen [verses].
taiḥ karmabhiḥ
By those actions.
sukhaṃ vānyasya suḥkhasyopaśamaṃ vety arthaḥ
Whether one obtains happiness or the cessation of another’s suffering—this is the meaning.
athavānyad vā na vindeta
Or whether one might find something else.
kiṃ tat ? ity apekṣāyāṃ tasyaiva nirdeśaḥ
When the question “what is that?” is expected, that very thing is specified.
upāramaṃ veti
Or cessation, meaning renunciation.
tatas taiḥ karmabhir bhūyaḥ punaḥ punar duḥkham eva vindeta
From those actions he would again and again obtain only suffering.
atraivaṃ vidhe saṃsāre no’smākaṃ yad yuktaṃ kartuṃ yogyaṃ tat-sarva-jño bhagavān vaden nirūpayatu
In this kind of world, may the omniscient Lord explain what is proper and fit for us to do.

entries.sanskrit: दैवात् प्राचीन-कर्मणो निमित्त-भूतात् कृष्णाद् विमुखस्यातोऽधर्म-शीलस्यातः सुदुःखितस्य जनस्यानुग्रहाय भव्यानि मङ्गलानि भूतानि चरन्ति । भवन्तः परोपकार-स्वभावा एवेत्य् अर्थः ॥३॥
word_for_word: daivāt prācīna-karmaṇo nimitta-bhūtāt kṛṣṇād vimukhasyāto’dharma-śīlasyātaḥ suduḥkhitasya janasyānugrahāya bhavyāni maṅgalāni bhūtāni caranti
Because of past action functioning as the cause, auspicious beings move for the compassion of a person who is averse to Kṛṣṇa, sinful in conduct and greatly afflicted.
bhavantaḥ paropakāra-svabhāvā evety arthaḥ
The meaning is that you have the nature of acting for the welfare of others.
entries.literal_english: Because of past action functioning as the cause, auspicious beings move for the compassion of a person who is averse to Kṛṣṇa, sinful in conduct and greatly afflicted. The meaning is that you have the nature of acting for the welfare of others.

entries.sanskrit: तत् तस्मात् हे साधु-वर्य, शं सुख-रूपं वर्त्म न आदिश कथय । येन वर्त्मना संराधितो हृदि-स्थितः सन् । स-तत्त्वाधिगम आत्मापारोक्ष्यं तत्-सहितम् । पुराणम् अनादि-वेद-प्रमाणकम् ॥४॥
word_for_word: tat tasmāt he sādhu-varya, śaṃ sukha-rūpaṃ vartma na ādiśa kathaya
Therefore, O best of the good, tell us the blissful path.
yena vartmanā saṃrādhito hṛdi-sthitaḥ san
By that path the Lord, situated in the heart, is pleased.
sa-tattvādhigama ātmāpārokṣyaṃ tat-sahitam
[He grants] knowledge together with realization of the truth and direct perception of the self.
purāṇam anādi-veda-pramāṇakam
The ancient Purāṇa, authoritative from the beginning like the Veda.

entries.sanskrit: करोति कर्माणीत्य्-आदीनां वर्णयेति पञ्चम-श्लोके क्रिया-संबन्धः । यथा येन प्रकारेण पुरुष-रूपेण कृतावतारः सन् त्र्य्-अधीशः त्रि-गुण-माया-नियन्ता, अतः स्व-तन्त्र एव, यानि कर्माणि करोति । कर्माण्य् एव विशेषतः पृच्छति---यथेत्य्-आदिना । निरीहो निष्क्रियो निःस्पृहो वा संस्थाप्य सु-स्थितं कृत्वा । वृत्तिं जीविकाम् ॥५॥
word_for_word: karoti karmāṇīty-ādīnāṃ varṇayeti pañcama-śloke kriyā-saṃbandhaḥ
The grammatical connection of the fifth verse is with “he performs the actions” and the like.
yathā yena prakāreṇa puruṣa-rūpeṇa kṛtāvatāraḥ san try-adhīśaḥ tri-guṇa-māyā-niyantā, ataḥ sva-tantra eva, yāni karmāṇi karoti
He particularly asks about the actions, beginning with “how.”
karmāṇy eva viśeṣataḥ pṛcchati---yathety-ādinā
Having established [the world] well, whether without desire, inactive or free from longing.
nirīho niṣkriyo niḥspṛho vā saṃsthāpya su-sthitaṃ kṛtvā
Livelihood, or means of subsistence.
vṛttiṃ jīvikām
This is the meaning of vṛtti.
entries.literal_english: The grammatical connection of the fifth verse is with “he performs the actions” and the like. He particularly asks about the actions, beginning with “how.” Having established [the world] well, whether without desire, inactive or free from longing. Livelihood, or means of subsistence. This is the meaning of vṛtti.

entries.sanskrit: स्वे स्वीये स्वे हृदयाकाशे निवेश्य स्थापयित्वा । निवृत्ता वृत्तयो यस्य । गुहायां योग-मायायाम् । बहुधा ब्रह्मादि-रूपेण ॥६॥
word_for_word: sve svīye sve hṛdayākāśe niveśya sthāpayitvā
Having placed this [universe] in his own heart-space.
nivṛttā vṛttayo yasya
Whose activities have ceased.
guhāyāṃ yoga-māyāyām
In the cave, namely in yogamāyā.
bahudhā brahmādi-rūpeṇa
In many forms, beginning with Brahmā.
entries.literal_english: Having placed this [universe] in his own heart-space. Whose activities have ceased. In the cave, namely in yogamāyā. In many forms, beginning with Brahmā.

entries.sanskrit: मत्स्याद्य्-अवतार-भेदैः क्रीडन् यानि यथा कर्माणि विधत्ते । पुनर् विशेषं प्रष्टुम् औत्सुक्यम् आविष्करोति---मन इति । सु-श्लोकाः पुण्य-कीर्तयः, तेषां मौलिर् इवाधिक्येनोपरि-विराजमानः, तस्येत्य् अर्थः ॥७॥
word_for_word: matsyādy-avatāra-bhedaiḥ krīḍan yāni yathā karmāṇi vidhatte
He performs whatever actions he performs while sporting through distinctions of incarnations beginning with Matsya.
punar viśeṣaṃ praṣṭum autsukyam āviṣkaroti---mana iti
He again reveals eagerness to ask specifically, beginning with “the mind.”
su-ślokāḥ puṇya-kīrtayaḥ, teṣāṃ maulir ivādhikyenopari-virājamānaḥ, tasyety arthaḥ
The Lord is the foremost, as it were the crest, of those of auspicious fame; that is the meaning.
entries.literal_english: He performs whatever actions he performs while sporting through distinctions of incarnations beginning with Matsya. He again reveals eagerness to ask specifically, beginning with “the mind.” The Lord is the foremost, as it were the crest, of those of auspicious fame; that is the meaning.

entries.sanskrit: अधिलोक-नाथो लोकनाथाधिपतिः । अलोकान् लोकालोक-पर्वताद् बहिर्-भागान् । अचीकॢपत् कल्पयाम् आस । यत्र येषु सर्वाणि यानि सत्त्वानि, तेषां निकायाः, तेषां भेदोऽधिकृतस् तत्-तत्-कर्माधिकारी आश्रित इति वा ॥८॥
word_for_word: adhiloka-nātho lokanāthādhipatiḥ
The lord above the lords of the worlds.
alokān lokāloka-parvatād bahir-bhāgān
The worlds outside the Lokāloka mountain.
acīkḷpat kalpayām āsa
He arranged and created them.
yatra yeṣu sarvāṇi yāni sattvāni, teṣāṃ nikāyāḥ, teṣāṃ bhedo’dhikṛtas tat-tat-karmādhikārī āśrita iti vā
In each place are the groups of beings, with their respective distinctions and authorities, or with the authorities assigned according to their actions.
entries.literal_english: The lord above the lords of the worlds. The worlds outside the Lokāloka mountain. He arranged and created them. In each place are the groups of beings, with their respective distinctions and authorities, or with the authorities assigned according to their actions.

entries.sanskrit: उतापि च येन प्रकारेण जीवानाम् आत्मा स्वभावस् तत्-कृतं कर्म तत्-कृतं रूपं तत्-कृता अभिधास् तासां भेदं कृतवान् । विश्व-स्रष्टा स्वयम् आत्म-योनिः स्वतः सिद्धः ॥९॥
word_for_word: utāpi ca yena prakāreṇa jīvānām ātmā svabhāvas tat-kṛtaṃ karma tat-kṛtaṃ rūpaṃ tat-kṛtā abhidhās tāsāṃ bhedaṃ kṛtavān
He also made the distinctions among the natures, actions, forms and names produced for the living beings.
viśva-sraṣṭā svayam ātma-yoniḥ svataḥ siddhaḥ
He is the self-born creator of the universe, self-established.
entries.literal_english: He also made the distinctions among the natures, actions, forms and names produced for the living beings. He is the self-born creator of the universe, self-established.

entries.sanskrit: ननु महाभारते त्वया सर्वं श्रुतम् एव, किं पुनः प्रश्नैः ? तत्राह---परे त्रैवर्णिका अवरे शूद्रादयः, तेषां व्रतानि धर्माः । मे मया । अभीक्ष्णं पुनः पुनः । तेषां श्रवणेनातृप्नुम तृप्ताः स्म । तेषां तुच्छ-सुखावहत्वात् । यस् तु तत्र कृष्ण-कथामृतौघः सूचितस् तस्माद् ऋते । तत्र त्व् अलं-बुद्धिर् नास्तीत्य् अर्थः ॥१०॥
word_for_word: nanu mahābhārate tvayā sarvaṃ śrutam eva, kiṃ punaḥ praśnaiḥ ? tatrāha---pare traivarṇikā avare śūdrādayaḥ, teṣāṃ vratāni dharmāḥ
You have indeed heard everything in the Mahābhārata; why ask again? The higher are the three varṇas and the lower are śūdras and others, whose vows are their duties.
me mayā
By me.
abhīkṣṇaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
Again and again.
teṣāṃ śravaṇenātṛpnuma tṛptāḥ sma
We became satisfied through hearing them.
teṣāṃ tuccha-sukhāvahatvāt
Because they bring only trivial happiness.
yas tu tatra kṛṣṇa-kathāmṛtaughaḥ sūcitas tasmād ṛte
Except for the stream of nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s topics indicated there.
tatra tv alaṃ-buddhir nāstīty arthaḥ
The meaning is that there is no complete interest there apart from Kṛṣṇa-kathā.
entries.literal_english: You have indeed heard everything in the Mahābhārata; why ask again? The higher are the three varṇas and the lower are śūdras and others, whose vows are their duties. By me. Again and again. We became satisfied through hearing them. Because they bring only trivial happiness. Except for the stream of nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s topics indicated there. The meaning is that there is no complete interest there apart from Kṛṣṇa-kathā.

entries.sanskrit: तत्र हेतुः---क इति । तीर्थ-पदः कृष्णस्य । अभिधानात् कथामृतौघात् । सत्रेषु समाजेषु । सूरिभिर् नारदादिभिः ॥११॥
word_for_word: tatra hetuḥ---ka iti
The reason is asked: “who?”
tīrtha-padaḥ kṛṣṇasya
Whose feet are the sacred ford—namely Kṛṣṇa’s.
abhidhānāt kathāmṛtaughāt
Because of the stream of nectar consisting of His name and narration.
satreṣu samājeṣu
In assemblies.
sūribhir nāradādibhiḥ
By sages such as Nārada.
entries.literal_english: The reason is asked: “who?” Whose feet are the sacred ford—namely Kṛṣṇa’s. Because of the stream of nectar consisting of His name and narration. In assemblies. By sages such as Nārada.

entries.sanskrit:
महाभारतस्याप्य् अत्रैव तात्पर्यम् इत्य् आह---मुनिः कृष्णो वेद-व्यासो भगवद्-गुणान् मोक्ष-धर्मान्ते नारायणीयाख्याने वक्तुम् इच्छुः सन् । अर्थ-कामादि-वर्णनं तु हरि-कथायां मति-प्रवेशार्थम् एवेत्य् आह---यस्मिन्न् इति । नृणां मतिर् ग्राम्य-सुखानुवादैर् द्वार-भूतैर् नु निश्चितं हरेः कथायां गृहीता नीता । तद् उक्तम् इतिहास-समुच्चये---

> कामिनो वर्णयन् कामान् लोभं लुब्धस्य वर्णयन् । >
> नरः किं फलम् आप्नोति कूपेऽन्धम् इव पातयन् । >
> लोक-चित्तावतारार्थं वर्णयित्वात्र तेन तौ । >
> इतिहासैः पवित्रार्थैः पुनर् अत्रैव निन्दितौ । >
> अन्यथा घोर-संसार-बन्ध-हेतू जनस्य तौ । >
> वर्णयेत् स कथं विद्वान् महा-कारुणिको मुनिः ॥ इति ॥१२॥
word_for_word: mahābhāratasyāpy atraiva tātparyam ity āha---muniḥ kṛṣṇo veda-vyāso bhagavad-guṇān mokṣa-dharmānte nārāyaṇīyākhyāne vaktum icchuḥ san
The purport of the Mahābhārata also lies here: the sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsa, desiring to speak the Lord’s qualities at the end of Mokṣa-dharma in the Nārāyaṇīya section...
artha-kāmādi-varṇanaṃ tu hari-kathāyāṃ mati-praveśārtham evety āha---yasminn iti
He says “in which” to show that descriptions of wealth and desire are only for introducing the mind to Hari’s narration.
nṛṇāṃ matir grāmya-sukhānuvādair dvāra-bhūtair nu niścitaṃ hareḥ kathāyāṃ gṛhītā nītā
People’s minds, through doors consisting of reports of worldly pleasures, are surely led into Hari’s narration.
tad uktam itihāsa-samuccaye---
This is stated in the compilation of histories:
kāmino varṇayan kāmān lobhaṃ lubdhasya varṇayan
What result does a man obtain by describing the desires of the lustful and the greed of the greedy?
naraḥ kiṃ phalam āpnoti kūpe’ndham iva pātayan
He throws him into a blind well.
loka-cittāvatārārthaṃ varṇayitvātra tena tau
He describes those two here to enter the minds of people.
itihāsaiḥ pavitrārthaiḥ punar atraiva ninditau
By histories whose meanings are sacred, he condemns those very two here again.
anyathā ghora-saṃsāra-bandha-hetū janasya tau
Otherwise, how could the greatly compassionate sage, knowing the truth, describe them as causes of terrible bondage in saṃsāra?
varṇayet sa kathaṃ vidvān mahā-kāruṇiko muniḥ
This is the conclusion of the quotation.
iti
This is what was stated.
entries.literal_english: The purport of the Mahābhārata also lies here: the sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsa, desiring to speak the Lord’s qualities at the end of Mokṣa-dharma in the Nārāyaṇīya section... He says “in which” to show that descriptions of wealth and desire are only for introducing the mind to Hari’s narration. People’s minds, through doors consisting of reports of worldly pleasures, are surely led into Hari’s narration. This is stated in the compilation of histories: What result does a man obtain by describing the desires of the lustful and the greed of the greedy? He throws him into a blind well. He describes those two here to enter the minds of people. By histories whose meanings are sacred, he condemns those very two here again. Otherwise, how could the greatly compassionate sage, knowing the truth, describe them as causes of terrible bondage in saṃsāra? This is the conclusion of the quotation. This is what was stated.

entries.sanskrit: श्री-हरि-कथायां मति-प्रवेशस्य फलम् आह---सा कथा मतिर् वा । अन्यत्र ग्राम्य-सुखे । ततः किम् ? अत आह---हरेर् इति ॥१३॥
word_for_word: śrī-hari-kathāyāṃ mati-praveśasya phalam āha---sā kathā matir vā
He states the result of entering the mind into the narration of Śrī Hari: “that narration becomes the mind.”
anyatra grāmya-sukhe
Elsewhere there is only the happiness of worldly life.
tataḥ kim ? ata āha---harer iti
What follows from that? He answers: it is the narration of Hari.
entries.literal_english: He states the result of entering the mind into the narration of Śrī Hari: “that narration becomes the mind.” Elsewhere there is only the happiness of worldly life. What follows from that? He answers: it is the narration of Hari.

entries.sanskrit: एवं-भूतायां कथायां ये न रमन्ते, तान् शोचति । शोच्या ये, तेषाम् अपि शोच्यांश् च । तत्राविदो भारत-तात्पर्यान् अभिज्ञान् शोच्यान् । ये तु ज्ञात्वापि हरेः कथायां विमुखाः, तांस् तेषाम् अपि शोच्यान् इति योज्यम् । अनिमिषः कालो येषाम् आयुः क्षिपति । अत्रैव हेतुः---वृथैव वाद-गति-स्मृतयो वाग्-देह-मनो-व्यापारा येषाम् ॥१४॥
word_for_word: evaṃ-bhūtāyāṃ kathāyāṃ ye na ramante, tān śocati
He laments those who do not delight in such narration.
śocyā ye, teṣām api śocyāṃś ca
Those who are pitiable, and even those who are more pitiable than them.
tatrāvido bhārata-tātparyān abhijñān śocyān
Among them, the ignorant who do not know the purport of the Bhārata are pitiable.
ye tu jñātvāpi hareḥ kathāyāṃ vimukhāḥ, tāṃs teṣām api śocyān iti yojyam
Those who, even after knowing it, are averse to Hari’s narration are also to be understood as pitiable.
animiṣaḥ kālo yeṣām āyuḥ kṣipati
Time without a blink carries away the life of such persons.
atraiva hetuḥ---vṛthaiva vāda-gati-smṛtayo vāg-deha-mano-vyāpārā yeṣām
The reason is that their speech, bodily activity and mental activity proceed uselessly in argument, wandering and memory.
entries.literal_english: He laments those who do not delight in such narration. Those who are pitiable, and even those who are more pitiable than them. Among them, the ignorant who do not know the purport of the Bhārata are pitiable. Those who, even after knowing it, are averse to Hari’s narration are also to be understood as pitiable. Time without a blink carries away the life of such persons. The reason is that their speech, bodily activity and mental activity proceed uselessly in argument, wandering and memory.

entries.sanskrit: तत् तस्माद् धे कौपारव ! अस्य विश्वस्य शिवाय कथासु सार-भूतां हरेः कथाम् एवोद्धृत्य नः कीर्तय । यथा पुष्पेभ्यो मधु मधुप उद्धरति तद्वद् उद्धृत्य ॥१५॥
word_for_word: tat tasmād dhe kaupārava ! asya viśvasya śivāya kathāsu sāra-bhūtāṃ hareḥ kathām evoddhṛtya naḥ kīrtaya
Therefore, O Kauṣārava, for the welfare of this world, extract and recite for us the essence of all narrations—the narration of Hari.
yathā puṣpebhyo madhu madhupa uddharati tadvad uddhṛtya
Just as a bee extracts honey from flowers, so extract it.
entries.literal_english: Therefore, O Kauṣārava, for the welfare of this world, extract and recite for us the essence of all narrations—the narration of Hari. Just as a bee extracts honey from flowers, so extract it.

entries.sanskrit: विशेषतः श्री-कृष्ण-कथा कथनीयेत्य् आशयेनाह---स इति । यो विश्व-सर्गाद्य्-अर्थं पूर्वं गृहीत-शक्तिः स एव पुरुषेषु कृतावतारः सन् पुरुषान् अतिक्रम्य वर्तमानानि यानि चकार तानि विस्तराद् वद ॥१६॥
word_for_word: viśeṣataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-kathā kathanīyety āśayenāha---sa iti
With the intention that the narration of Śrī Kṛṣṇa should especially be spoken, he says “He.”
yo viśva-sargādy-arthaṃ pūrvaṃ gṛhīta-śaktiḥ sa eva puruṣeṣu kṛtāvatāraḥ san puruṣān atikramya vartamānāni yāni cakāra tāni vistarād vada
He who first received power for the creation of the universe and then incarnated among the Puruṣas—describe at length the deeds He performed beyond the Puruṣas.
entries.literal_english: With the intention that the narration of Śrī Kṛṣṇa should especially be spoken, he says “He.” He who first received power for the creation of the universe and then incarnated among the Puruṣas—describe at length the deeds He performed beyond the Puruṣas.

entries.sanskrit: पुंसां निःश्रेयसम् एवार्थः प्रयोजनं तेन हेतुना पृष्टः ॥१७॥

the supreme benefit of all people alone
tena hetunā pṛṣṭaḥ
for that reason he was asked
entries.literal_english: The benefit of all people alone is the purpose; for that reason he was asked.

entries.sanskrit: बहु-मानम् एवाह---साध्व् इति पञ्चभिः । अधोक्षजे एवात्मा मनो यस्य तस्यात्मनः स्वस्य कीर्तिं च प्रसङ्गाद् वितन्वता ॥१८॥
word_for_word: bahu-mānam evāha---sādhv iti pañcabhiḥ
He expresses great honor, beginning with “well,” in five verses.
adhokṣaje evātmā mano yasya tasyātmanaḥ svasya kīrtiṃ ca prasaṅgād vitanvatā
By him whose mind is fixed only on Adhokṣaja, while also expanding the fame of his own self in the process.

entries.sanskrit: हरिर् यद् गृहीतः एतच् चित्रं न भवति । कुतः ? बादरायण-वीर्यजो धृतराष्ट्रोऽपि भवति, सत्यम्, परन्तु त्वयि ततो विशेष इत्य् आह---गृहीत इति ॥१९॥
word_for_word: harir yad gṛhītaḥ etac citraṃ na bhavati
There is nothing astonishing if Hari has been accepted by you.
kutaḥ ? bādarāyaṇa-vīryajo dhṛtarāṣṭro’pi bhavati, satyam, parantu tvayi tato viśeṣa ity āha---gṛhīta iti
Why? Dhṛtarāṣṭra too was born from the seed of Bādarāyaṇa; that is true, but he says that you are especially distinguished from him: “accepted.”
entries.literal_english: There is nothing astonishing if Hari has been accepted by you. Why? Dhṛtarāṣṭra too was born from the seed of Bādarāyaṇa; that is true, but he says that you are especially distinguished from him: “accepted.”

entries.sanskrit: ननु तर्हि कथं शूद्रत्वं ? कथं च लोकानुग्राहकत्वं ? तत्राह---माण्डव्य-शापाद् इति । भ्रातुर् विचित्रवीर्यस्य क्षेत्रे क्षेत्रत्वेन स्वीकृतायां भुजिष्यायां दास्यां यम एव त्वं जातोऽसि ॥२०॥
word_for_word: nanu tarhi kathaṃ śūdratvaṃ ? kathaṃ ca lokānugrāhakatvaṃ ? tatrāha---māṇḍavya-śāpād iti
Then how are you a śūdra, and how are you one who benefits the world? He answers: “because of Māṇḍavya’s curse.”
bhrātur vicitravīryasya kṣetre kṣetratvena svīkṛtāyāṃ bhujiṣyāyāṃ dāsyāṃ yama eva tvaṃ jāto’si
You were born as Yama himself in the maidservant accepted as the field of your brother Vicitravīrya.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, भवान् इति । कुतः ? यस्य तव ज्ञानोपदेशाय माम् आदिष्टवान् । च-कारात् स्वयम् अपि स्मृत्यैवोपदिष्टवान् इति ॥२१॥
word_for_word: kiṃ ca, bhavān iti

kutaḥ ? yasya tava jñānopadeśāya mām ādiṣṭavān

ca-kārāt svayam api smṛtyaivopadiṣṭavān iti
By the conjunction, it is also understood that he instructed you himself merely by remembering.

entries.sanskrit:
तत्र सृष्टि-लीलां वर्णयितुं ततः पूर्वावस्थाम् आह---इदं विश्वम् अग्रे सृष्टेः पूर्वं परमात्मा भगवान् एक एव आस आसीत् । आत्मनां जीवानाम् आत्मा स्वरूपं विभुः स्वामी च । नान्यद् द्रष्टृ-दृश्यात्मकं किञ्चिद् आसीत् ।

कारणात्मना सत्त्वेऽपि पृथक् प्रतीत्य्-अभावाद् इत्य् आह---नाना-मत्य्-उपलक्षणो नाना-द्रष्टृ-दृश्यादि-मतिभिर् नोपलक्ष्यत इति तथा। यद् वा, अ-कार-प्रश्लेषं विनैवायम् अर्थः । यः सृष्टौ नाना-मतिभिर् उपलक्ष्यते, स तदैक एवासीद् इति । कुतः ? आत्मेच्छा माया तस्या अनुगतौ लये सति । यद् वा, आत्मन एकाकित्वेनावस्थानेच्छायाम् अनुवृत्तायाम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२३॥
word_for_word: tatra sṛṣṭi-līlāṃ varṇayituṃ tataḥ pūrvāvasthām āha---idaṃ viśvam agre sṛṣṭeḥ pūrvaṃ paramātmā bhagavān eka eva āsa āsīt
To describe the creation-pastime, he first describes the prior state: before creation, the Supreme Self, the Lord, alone existed.
ātmanāṃ jīvānām ātmā svarūpaṃ vibhuḥ svāmī ca
The self of the living beings, their essential nature, and their Lord.
nānyad draṣṭṛ-dṛśyātmakaṃ kiñcid āsīt
Nothing else consisting of seer and seen existed.
kāraṇātmanā sattve’pi pṛthak pratīty-abhāvād ity āha---nānā-maty-upalakṣaṇo nānā-draṣṭṛ-dṛśyādi-matibhir nopalakṣyata iti tathā
Because even in the causal state there was no separate perception, he says that it was not marked by various seers, objects and viewpoints.
yad vā, a-kāra-praśleṣaṃ vinaivāyam arthaḥ
Or this meaning is obtained without inserting the privative a.
yaḥ sṛṣṭau nānā-matibhir upalakṣyate, sa tadaika evāsīd iti
That which in creation is recognized through various viewpoints was then alone.
kutaḥ ? ātmecchā māyā tasyā anugatau laye sati
Why? Māyā is the self’s will; when she was dissolved into it.
yad vā, ātmana ekākitvenāvasthānecchāyām anuvṛttāyām ity arthaḥ
Or, the meaning is that the desire to remain alone in the Self continued.

Māyā is the self’s will; when she was dissolved into it. Or, the meaning is that the desire to remain alone in the Self continued.

entries.sanskrit: तत्र प्रथमं मायोद्भव-प्रकारम् आह द्वाभ्याम् । स वै एष द्रष्टा सन् दृश्य नापश्यत् । यत एक-राट् एक एव तदा प्रकाशते । आत्मानम् असन्तम् इव मेने । दृश्याभावे द्रष्टृत्वाभावात् । तदाह---सुप्ता मायाद्याः शक्तयो यस्य सः । न त्व् असन्तम् एव मेने । यतोऽसुप्ता दृक् चिच्-छक्तिर् यस्येति ॥२४॥
word_for_word: tatra prathamaṃ māyodbhava-prakāram āha dvābhyām
Here he first explains the manner in which māyā arose, in two verses.
sa vai eṣa draṣṭā san dṛśya nāpaśyat
Although he was the seer, he did not see the object.
yata eka-rāṭ eka eva tadā prakāśate
Because only the one sovereign shone at that time.
ātmānam asantam iva mene
He considered himself as though nonexistent.
dṛśyābhāve draṣṭṛtvābhāvāt
Because when the object is absent, seerhood is absent.
tadāha---suptā māyādyāḥ śaktayo yasya saḥ
Therefore he says: whose powers beginning with māyā were dormant.
na tv asantam eva mene
It is not that he considered himself truly nonexistent.
yato’suptā dṛk cic-chaktir yasyeti
Because his seeing, conscious power was not dormant.
entries.literal_english: Here he first explains the manner in which māyā arose, in two verses. Although he was the seer, he did not see the object. Because only the one sovereign shone at that time. He considered himself as though nonexistent. Because when the object is absent, seerhood is absent. Therefore he says: whose powers beginning with māyā were dormant. It is not that he considered himself truly nonexistent. Because his seeing, conscious power was not dormant.

entries.sanskrit: सा वै दृअष्टृ-दृश्यानुसन्धान-रूपा ।सद्दृश्यम्,असद् अदृश्यम् । आत्मा स्वरूपम् । सद्-असतोर् आत्मा यस्याः, तद्-उभयानुसन्धान-रूपत्वात् ॥२५॥
word_for_word: sā vai dṛaṣṭṛ-dṛśyānusandhāna-rūpā saddṛśyam,asad adṛśyam
Māyā is of the nature of investigating the seer and the seen.
ātmā svarūpam
The existent is seen; the nonexistent is unseen.
sad-asator ātmā yasyāḥ, tad-ubhayānusandhāna-rūpatvāt
The self is the essential nature, and she investigates both the existent and the nonexistent.
entries.literal_english: Māyā is of the nature of investigating the seer and the seen. The existent is seen; the nonexistent is unseen. The self is the essential nature, and she investigates both the existent and the nonexistent.

word_for_word: kāla-vṛttyā kāla-śaktyā guṇa-mayyāṃ kṣubhita-guṇāyām
By the activity of time, namely the power of time, in māyā made of the guṇas whose guṇas were agitated.
adhokṣajaḥ paramātmā
Adhokṣaja, the Supreme Self.
ātmāṃśa-bhūtena puruṣeṇa prakṛty-adhiṣṭhātṛ-rūpeṇa vīryaṃ cid-ābhāsam ādhatta
Through the Puruṣa who is His own portion and presides over material nature, He placed the seed, the reflection of consciousness.
vīryavāṃś cic-chakti-yuktaḥ
“Possessing potency” means endowed with cit-śakti.
entries.literal_english: By the activity of time, namely the power of time, in māyā made of the guṇas whose guṇas were agitated. Adhokṣaja, the Supreme Self. Through the Puruṣa who is His own portion and presides over material nature, He placed the seed, the reflection of consciousness. “Possessing potency” means endowed with cit-śakti.

entries.sanskrit:
काल-प्रेरिताद् अव्यक्तान् मायातः । तत्त्व-पदं परित्यज्य महतो लक्षणम्, अतः पुंलिङ्ग-निर्देशो विज्ञानात्मेति । सत्त्व-प्रधानत्वात् स्व-देह-स्थं विश्वम् उच्छून-बीज-गतम् अङ्कुरादि-रूपं वृक्षम् इव व्यञ्जन् व्यञ्जयन् प्रकाशयन् । यतोऽसौ तमो नुदतीति तमो-नुदः । तद् उक्तं सात्वत-तन्त्रे---

> विष्णोस् तु त्रीणि रूपाणि पुरुषाख्यान्य् अथो विदुः । >
> प्रथमं महतः स्रष्टृ द्वितीयं त्व् अण्ड-संस्थितम् । >
> तृतीयं सर्व-भूत-स्थं तानि ज्ञात्वा विमुच्यते ॥ इति ॥२७॥
word_for_word: kāla-preritād avyaktān māyātaḥ
From unmanifest māyā impelled by time.
tattva-padaṃ parityajya mahato lakṣaṇam, ataḥ puṃliṅga-nirdeśo vijñānātmeti
Abandoning the neuter word tattva, the text uses the masculine designation vijñānātmā to indicate mahat.
sattva-pradhānatvāt sva-deha-sthaṃ viśvam ucchūna-bīja-gatam aṅkurādi-rūpaṃ vṛkṣam iva vyañjan vyañjayan prakāśayan
Because he manifests the universe situated in his own body, like a tree with its sprout hidden in a seed.
yato’sau tamo nudatīti tamo-nudaḥ
Because he dispels darkness, he is called the dispeller of darkness.
tad uktaṃ sātvata-tantre---
This is stated in the Sātvata-tantra:
viṣṇos tu trīṇi rūpāṇi puruṣākhyāny atho viduḥ
They know three forms of Viṣṇu called Puruṣa.
prathamaṃ mahataḥ sraṣṭṛ dvitīyaṃ tv aṇḍa-saṃsthitam
The first is the creator of mahat; the second is situated in the cosmic egg.
tṛtīyaṃ sarva-bhūta-sthaṃ tāni jñātvā vimucyate
The third is present in all beings; knowing these, one is liberated.
iti
Thus.
entries.literal_english: From unmanifest māyā impelled by time. Abandoning the neuter word tattva, the text uses the masculine designation vijñānātmā to indicate mahat. Because he manifests the universe situated in his own body, like a tree with its sprout hidden in a seed. Because he dispels darkness, he is called the dispeller of darkness. This is stated in the Sātvata-tantra: They know three forms of Viṣṇu called Puruṣa. The first is the creator of mahat; the second is situated in the cosmic egg. The third is present in all beings; knowing these, one is liberated. Thus.

entries.sanskrit: अहङ्कारोत्पत्तिम् आह सार्धाभ्याम्, सोऽपीति । अंशश् चिद्-आभासो निमित्तं, गुणा उपादानं, कालः क्षोभकः, तद्-आत्मा तद्-अधीनः भगवान् सर्वाध्यक्षस् तद्-दृष्टि-गोचरः सन् स्वयम् आत्मानं व्यकरोत् रूपान्तरम् अनयत् ॥२८॥
word_for_word: ahaṅkārotpattim āha sārdhābhyām, so’pīti
He explains the arising of ahaṅkāra in one and a half verses, beginning with “he too.”
aṃśaś cid-ābhāso nimittaṃ, guṇā upādānaṃ, kālaḥ kṣobhakaḥ, tad-ātmā tad-adhīnaḥ bhagavān sarvādhyakṣas tad-dṛṣṭi-gocaraḥ san svayam ātmānaṃ vyakarot rūpāntaram anayat

The conscious reflection is the instrumental cause, the guṇas are the material cause, time agitates them, and the Lord, whose self is dependent on them and who oversees all, transformed Himself into another form.
entries.literal_english: He explains the arising of ahaṅkāra in one and a half verses, beginning with “he too.” The conscious reflection is the instrumental cause, the guṇas are the material cause, time agitates them, and the Lord, whose self is dependent on them and who oversees all, transformed Himself into another form.

entries.sanskrit: अहङ्कारस्य लक्षणम् आह---कार्यम् अधिभूतम्, कारणम् अध्यात्मम्, कर्तृ अधिदैवं, तेषाम् आत्मा आश्रयः । अत्र हेतुः, भूतेन्द्रिय-मनो-मयस् तद्-विकारवान् । मन इति देवानाम् अप्य् उपलक्षणम् ॥२९॥
word_for_word: ahaṅkārasya lakṣaṇam āha---kāryam adhibhūtam, kāraṇam adhyātmam, kartṛ adhidaivaṃ, teṣām ātmā āśrayaḥ
He states the definition of ahaṅkāra: the effect is adhibhūta, the cause is adhyātma, the agent is adhidaiva, and their self is the supporting basis.
atra hetuḥ, bhūtendriya-mano-mayas tad-vikāravān
The reason is that it consists of the elements, senses and mind and possesses their transformations.
mana iti devānām apy upalakṣaṇam
“Mind” also serves as an indication of the deities.

The reason is that it consists of the elements, senses and mind and possesses their transformations. “Mind” also serves as an indication of the deities.

entries.sanskrit: एतद् एव विभागतः प्रपञ्चयति---वैकारिक इत्य्-आदिना । वैकारिकः सात्त्विकः, तैजसो राजसः । देवाश् च वैकारिकाः, सात्त्विकाहङ्कार-कार्य-भूता इत्य् अर्थः । यतो येभ्य इन्द्रियाधिष्ठातृभ्यो देवेभ्यो हेतु-भोऽर्थाभिव्यञ्जनं शब्दादि-प्रकाशो भवति ॥३०॥
word_for_word: etad eva vibhāgataḥ prapañcayati---vaikārika ity-ādinā
He elaborates this very division, beginning with “vaikārika.”
vaikārikaḥ sāttvikaḥ, taijaso rājasaḥ
Vaikārika is sāttvika; taijasa is rājasa.
devāś ca vaikārikāḥ, sāttvikāhaṅkāra-kārya-bhūtā ity arthaḥ
The gods are also vaikārika, being products of the sāttvika ahaṅkāra.
yato yebhya indriyādhiṣṭhātṛbhyo devebhyo hetu-bho’rthābhivyañjanaṃ śabdādi-prakāśo bhavati
Because from the deities presiding over the senses, who are the causes, the manifestation of objects—sound and the rest—takes place.

Because from the deities presiding over the senses, who are the causes, the manifestation of objects—sound and the rest—takes place.

entries.sanskrit: तैजसान्य् एवेत्य् अन्वयः । ज्ञान-मयानां सात्त्विकत्व-शङ्का मा भूद् इत्य् एव-कारः। तामसो भूत-सूक्ष्मस्य शब्दस्यादिः कारणम् । यतः शब्दात् खम् आकाशो भवति । आत्मनो लिङ्गं स्व-गुण-शब्द-रूपेण प्रकाशकं हृदयाकाशतया वा । यद् वा, लिङ्गं शरीरम् आकाश-शरीरं ब्रह्म इति श्रुतेः ॥३१॥
word_for_word: taijasāny evety anvayaḥ
The construction is “they are indeed taijasa.”
jñāna-mayānāṃ sāttvikatva-śaṅkā mā bhūd ity eva-kāraḥ
The emphatic particle prevents the doubt that knowledge, being conscious, is sāttvika.
tāmaso bhūta-sūkṣmasya śabdasyādiḥ kāraṇam
The tāmasa ego is the original cause of the subtle element, sound.
yataḥ śabdāt kham ākāśo bhavati
From sound arises space.
ātmano liṅgaṃ sva-guṇa-śabda-rūpeṇa prakāśakaṃ hṛdayākāśatayā vā
The liṅga of the Self is that which reveals it through its own quality, sound, or as the space of the heart.
yad vā, liṅgaṃ śarīram ākāśa-śarīraṃ brahma iti śruteḥ
Or liṅga means body, in accordance with the śruti “Brahman is space-bodied.”

entries.sanskrit: हे भव्य विदुर । पाठान्तरे भाव्यं कार्यम् । यद् यद् अवरम् अवरं कार्यं तेषां कार्याणां परैः कारणैर् अनुसंसर्गाद् यथा-सङ्ख्यं यथाक्रमम् उत्तरोत्तरम् अधिकान् गुणान् विदुः । तथाहि नभसः शब्द एव गुणोऽन्यान्वयाभावात् । वायोस् तु स्पर्श आकाशान्वयाच् छब्दश् च । एवं तैजसस् तौ च रूपं च । अम्भसस् तानि रसश् च । मह्याः सर्वे ॥३६॥
word_for_word: he bhavya vidura
O gentle Vidura.
pāṭhāntare bhāvyaṃ kāryam
With the alternative reading, bhāvya means the product.
yad yad avaram avaraṃ kāryaṃ teṣāṃ kāryāṇāṃ paraiḥ kāraṇair anusaṃsargād yathā-saṅkhyaṃ yathākramam uttarottaram adhikān guṇān viduḥ
Each lower product knows successively more qualities through contact with the higher causes.
tathāhi nabhasaḥ śabda eva guṇo’nyānvayābhāvāt
Space has sound alone as its quality because it has no connection with the other causes.
vāyos tu sparśa ākāśānvayāc chabdaś ca
Air has touch, and also sound because it retains space.
evaṃ taijasas tau ca rūpaṃ ca
Fire has those two qualities and also form.
ambhasas tāni rasaś ca
Water has those qualities and also taste.
mahyāḥ sarve
Earth has all of them.

Space has sound alone as its quality because it has no connection with the other causes. Air has touch, and also sound because it retains space. Fire has those two qualities and also form. Water has those qualities and also taste. Earth has all of them.

entries.sanskrit: भूतानाम् इति । आकाशादीनां पञ्चभूतानां यद् यत् परम् अपरं च कार्यम् । तेषां कार्याणां परैः कारणैर् अनुसंसर्गाद् अन्वयात् यथा-सङ्ख्यं यथा-क्रमम् उत्तर-उत्तरम् अधिकान् गुणान् विदुः । तथा हि नभसः शब्द एव गुणः, अन्यान्वयाभावात् । वायोस् तु स्पर्शः, आकाशान्वयात् शब्दश् च । एवं तेजसस् तौ च रूपं च । अम्भसस् तानि, रसश् च । मह्याः सर्वे । ‘भव्य’ इति पाठे विदुर !
word_for_word: bhūtānām iti
It says: “Of the elements.”
ākāśādīnāṃ pañcabhūtānāṃ yad yat param aparaṃ ca kāryam
Of the five elements beginning with space, each product, higher or lower, is meant.
teṣāṃ kāryāṇāṃ paraiḥ kāraṇair anusaṃsargād anvayāt yathā-saṅkhyaṃ yathā-kramam uttara-uttaram adhikān guṇān viduḥ
Through contact with the higher causes, the products know successively more qualities.
tathā hi nabhasaḥ śabda eva guṇaḥ, anyānvayābhāvāt
Thus space has sound alone, because it has no relation to other causes.
vāyos tu sparśaḥ, ākāśānvayāt śabdaś ca
Air has touch and also sound because it retains space.
evaṃ tejasas tau ca rūpaṃ ca
Fire has those two qualities and also form.
ambhasas tāni, rasaś ca
Water has those qualities and also taste.
mahyāḥ sarve
Earth has all the qualities.
‘bhavya’ iti pāṭhe vidura !
With the reading bhāvya, O Vidura, the word means the product.

Air has touch and also sound because it retains space. Fire has those two qualities and also form. Water has those qualities and also taste. Earth has all the qualities. With the reading bhāvya, O Vidura, the word means the product.

entries.sanskrit: मिथः स्पर्धिष्णवो देवान् अमिलन्तः परस्परम् । विश्व-कर्मण्य् अनीशाना निर्विण्णा हरिम् ईडिरे---नमामेति । प्रपन्नानां तापोपशमे । आतपत्रं छत्रम् । तत्र हेतुः---यस्य पादारविन्दस्य मूलं तलं केत आश्रयो येषां ते । संसार-दुःखं बहिर् दूरत उत्क्षिपन्ति परित्यजन्ति । पान्थाः स्व-गृहं प्राप्य मार्ग-श्रमम् इव ॥३८॥
word_for_word: mithaḥ spardhiṣṇavo devān amilantaḥ parasparam
The gods, mutually competing, did not unite with one another.
viśva-karmaṇy anīśānā nirviṇṇā harim īḍire---namāmeti
Unable to perform the work of the universe and distressed, they praised Hari: “We bow.”
prapannānāṃ tāpopaśame
For the alleviation of the distress of the surrendered.
ātapatraṃ chatram
An umbrella or shade.
tatra hetuḥ---yasya pādāravindasya mūlaṃ talaṃ keta āśrayo yeṣāṃ te
Those whose refuge is the base of His lotus feet.
saṃsāra-duḥkhaṃ bahir dūrata utkṣipanti parityajanti
They cast material suffering far away.
pānthāḥ sva-gṛhaṃ prāpya mārga-śramam iva
Like travelers who, having reached home, leave behind the fatigue of the road.

entries.sanskrit: श्रमं विनिवेदयन्त आहुः । हे धातः पितः, यत् यस्माद् भवे संसारे । आत्मन्न् आत्मनि । संबोधनं वा । शर्म सुखम् । "ऋते" यद् इति पाठे यत् पाद-भजनं विना शर्म न लभन्ते । ननु ज्ञानाद् अज्ञान-कृतस् तापो निवर्तते, किं मद्-अङ्घ्रि-च्छायाश्रयणेन तत्राहुः । स-विद्यां तद्-आश्रयणम् एव विद्या-प्रापकम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३९॥
word_for_word: śramaṃ vinivedayanta āhuḥ
They express their fatigue.
he dhātaḥ pitaḥ, yat yasmād bhave saṃsāre
O creator, O father, because in material existence...
ātmann ātmani
“O self,” in the self—or it is a vocative.
saṃbodhanaṃ vā
It is a form of address.
śarma sukham
Happiness.
"ṛte" yad iti pāṭhe yat pāda-bhajanaṃ vinā śarma na labhante
With the reading “ṛte,” they do not obtain happiness without worship of the feet.
nanu jñānād ajñāna-kṛtas tāpo nivartate, kiṃ mad-aṅghri-cchāyāśrayaṇena tatrāhuḥ
If knowledge removes the suffering caused by ignorance, why take shelter of the shade of My feet? He answers: taking shelter of it together with knowledge itself bestows knowledge.
sa-vidyāṃ tad-āśrayaṇam eva vidyā-prāpakam ity arthaḥ
That is the meaning.

entries.sanskrit: अज्ञातस्याश्रयणायोगात् तज्-ज्ञान-साधनम् आहुः । मार्गन्ति अन्वेषयन्ति यत् तत् तीर्थ-पदस् तव पदं वयं प्रपन्नाः । कैर् मार्गन्ति ? छन्दः-सुपर्णैर् वेद-पक्षिभिः । तवैव मुख-पद्मं नीडं येषाम् । यथा पक्षिणो नीडाद् उद्गताः, ततस् ततः परिभ्रम्य पुनस् तत्रैव विशन्ति, तथा वेदा अपि त्वत्त उद्गतास् त्वय्य् एव पर्यवस्यन्ति । अतो वेदानाश्रित्य त्वत्-पदं मृगयन्त इति । विविक्ते असङ्गे मनसि । किं च, अघ-मर्षम् अघ-नाशक-मुदम् उदकं यासां सरितां तासु वराया गङ्गायाः पदम् उद्गम-स्थानम् । अतो गङ्गाम् अनुसेवमाना अपि तद् उद्गम-स्थानं त्वत्-पदं प्राप्नुवन्तीत्य् अर्थः ॥४०॥
word_for_word: ajñātasyāśrayaṇāyogāt taj-jñāna-sādhanam āhuḥ
Since one cannot take shelter of what is unknown, they state the means of knowing it.
mārganti anveṣayanti yat tat tīrtha-padas tava padaṃ vayaṃ prapannāḥ
We have surrendered to Your sacred feet, which they seek.
kair mārganti ? chandaḥ-suparṇair veda-pakṣibhiḥ
With what do they seek? With the Vedic meters, the birds of the Veda.
tavaiva mukha-padmaṃ nīḍaṃ yeṣām
Your lotus mouth is their nest.
yathā pakṣiṇo nīḍād udgatāḥ, tatas tataḥ paribhramya punas tatraiva viśanti, tathā vedā api tvatta udgatās tvayy eva paryavasyanti
Just as birds emerge from a nest, wander and return there, so the Vedas arise from You and culminate in You.
ato vedānāśritya tvat-padaṃ mṛgayanta iti
Therefore they seek Your feet by taking shelter of the Vedas.
vivikte asaṅge manasi
In a mind free from attachment.
kiṃ ca, agha-marṣam agha-nāśaka-mudam udakaṃ yāsāṃ saritāṃ tāsu varāyā gaṅgāyāḥ padam udgama-sthānam
The Ganges is the source of rivers whose water destroys sin and gives joy.
ato gaṅgām anusevamānā api tad udgama-sthānaṃ tvat-padaṃ prāpnuvantīty arthaḥ
Thus, serving the Ganges, they reach its source, Your feet.

entries.sanskrit: ननु विषयाकृष्ट-चित्तानां कुतस् तद्-अन्वेषणं ? तत्राहुः---यद्-धृदयेऽवधाय ध्यात्वा, वैराग्यं बलं यस्य तेन ज्ञानेन धीरा भवन्ति । स-रागे चित्ते ध्यानम् एव कुतः ? तत्राहुः---श्रद्धया श्रवण-पूर्विकया भक्त्या च संमृज्यमाने संशोध्यमाने ॥४१॥
word_for_word: nanu viṣayākṛṣṭa-cittānāṃ kutas tad-anveṣaṇaṃ ? tatrāhuḥ---yad-dhṛdaye’vadhāya dhyātvā, vairāgyaṃ balaṃ yasya tena jñānena dhīrā bhavanti
How can those whose minds are drawn to sense objects seek that? He answers: having placed Him in the heart and meditated, the steadfast become so through knowledge whose strength is detachment.
sa-rāge citte dhyānam eva kutaḥ ? tatrāhuḥ---śraddhayā śravaṇa-pūrvikayā bhaktyā ca saṃmṛjyamāne saṃśodhyamāne
How can meditation exist in a mind full of attachment? He answers: through faith and devotion preceded by hearing, as the mind is cleansed.

entries.sanskrit: अन्तर्यामितया नित्यं सन्निहितेऽनर्थकं व्रजनम् इत्य् आशङ्क्याहुः---यद् इति । सानुबन्धे सोपकरणे । असति तुच्छे । पुर्यां स्व-देह एव वसतोऽपि । यत् सुदूरं दुष्प्रापम् ॥४३॥
word_for_word: antaryāmitayā nityaṃ sannihite’narthakaṃ vrajanam ity āśaṅkyāhuḥ---yad iti
Fearing that going would be pointless when He is always present as the indwelling controller, they say this.
sānubandhe sopakaraṇe
With all connections and equipment.
asati tucche
When absent, insignificant.
puryāṃ sva-deha eva vasato’pi
Although He dwells in the city of one’s own body.
yat sudūraṃ duṣprāpam
What is very far and difficult to attain.

entries.sanskrit:
ननु यदि हृदि-स्थस्यापि पदाब्जं केषाञ्चित् सुदूरं, तर्ह्य् अन्येषाम् अपि तथैव स्याद् अविशेषाद् इत्य् आशङ्क्याहुः---तान् इति । असद्-वृत्तिभिर् बहिर्-मुखैर् अक्षिभिर् इन्द्रियैः पराहृतं दूरम् अपहृतम् अन्तः-स्थं मनो येषां ते । अथो अत एव ते नूनं तान् न पश्यन्ति। वै प्रसिद्धम् । कुतः पुनस् तेषां तत्-सङ्गः स्यात् ? कान् ? ते तव पद-न्यासो गमनं, तस्य विलासो विभ्रमस्, तस्य लक्ष्मीः शोभा, तस्या ये, त्वल्-लीला-कथादिभिः शोभमानांस् त्वद्-भक्तान् इत्य् अर्थः ।

"पथ" इति "लक्ष्या" इति च पाठे त्वत्-पद-न्यास-विलासो लक्ष्यो येषां तान् । पथस् त्वन्-मार्ग-भूतान् सतो मार्गान् वा श्रवणादीन् न पश्यन्तीत्य् अर्थः। यद् वा, ये एवं-भूता भागवतास् ते तान् उन्मत्तान् नूनं नैव पश्यन्तीत्य् अन्वयः । सत्-सङ्गाभावेन हरि-कथा-श्रवणाभावाद् धृदि स्थितम् अपि तेषां सुदूरम् इति भावः ॥४४॥
word_for_word: nanu yadi hṛdi-sthasyāpi padābjaṃ keṣāñcit sudūraṃ, tarhy anyeṣām api tathaiva syād aviśeṣād ity āśaṅkyāhuḥ---tān iti
If the lotus feet situated in the heart are far for some, then the same would be true for others; therefore they say this.
asad-vṛttibhir bahir-mukhair akṣibhir indriyaiḥ parāhṛtaṃ dūram apahṛtam antaḥ-sthaṃ mano yeṣāṃ te
Their minds have been carried outward and far away by sinful conduct and the senses.
atho ata eva te nūnaṃ tān na paśyanti
Therefore they certainly do not see those feet.
vai prasiddham
Indeed, this is well known.
kutaḥ punas teṣāṃ tat-saṅgaḥ syāt ? kān ? te tava pada-nyāso gamanaṃ, tasya vilāso vibhramas, tasya lakṣmīḥ śobhā, tasyā ye, tval-līlā-kathādibhiḥ śobhamānāṃs tvad-bhaktān ity arthaḥ
Who are they? The devotees beautified by the splendor of Your footstep and by accounts of Your pastimes.
"patha" iti "lakṣyā" iti ca pāṭhe tvat-pada-nyāsa-vilāso lakṣyo yeṣāṃ tān
With the reading “path” and “goal,” they are those for whom the splendor of Your footstep is visible.
pathas tvan-mārga-bhūtān sato mārgān vā śravaṇādīn na paśyantīty arthaḥ
They do not see the paths that are Your way, or the practices such as hearing.
yad vā, ye evaṃ-bhūtā bhāgavatās te tān unmattān nūnaṃ naiva paśyantīty anvayaḥ
Or, those Bhagavatas do not see those mad people.
sat-saṅgābhāvena hari-kathā-śravaṇābhāvād dhṛdi sthitam api teṣāṃ sudūram iti bhāvaḥ
Because they lack saintly association and hearing Hari’s narration, the feet within their hearts seem far away.

entries.sanskrit: एतद् एव स्फुटयन्ति---पानेनेति द्वाभ्याम् । वैराग्यं सारो बलं यस्य बोधस्य तं लब्ध्वा । अन्वीयुः प्राप्नुयुः । अकुण्ठ-धिष्ण्यं वैकुण्ठ-लोकम् ॥४५॥
word_for_word: etad eva sphuṭayanti---pāneneti dvābhyām
They make this clear in two verses, beginning with “by drinking.”
vairāgyaṃ sāro balaṃ yasya bodhasya taṃ labdhvā
Having obtained knowledge whose strength is detachment.
anvīyuḥ prāpnuyuḥ
They attain it.
akuṇṭha-dhiṣṇyaṃ vaikuṇṭha-lokam
The unimpeded abode, the world of Vaikuṇṭha.
entries.literal_english: They make this clear in two verses, beginning with “by drinking.” Having obtained knowledge whose strength is detachment. They attain it. The unimpeded abode, the world of Vaikuṇṭha.

entries.sanskrit: आत्मनि समाधिर् मनः-स्थैर्यं स एव योग उपायः, तस्य बलेन । ज्ञान-योगतः श्रमेण मोक्षः सत्-सङ्गतस् त्वत्-कथा-श्रवणादिना त्व् अनायासेनैव । अहं ममताविष्टानां तु न कथञ्चिद् इति भावः ॥४६॥
word_for_word: ātmani samādhir manaḥ-sthairyaṃ sa eva yoga upāyaḥ, tasya balena
Samādhi in the Self is steadiness of mind; by the strength of that yoga means.
jñāna-yogataḥ śrameṇa mokṣaḥ sat-saṅgatas tvat-kathā-śravaṇādinā tv anāyāsenaiva
Liberation through the effort of the yoga of knowledge, but through saintly association and hearing Your topics it comes without effort.
ahaṃ mamatāviṣṭānāṃ tu na kathañcid iti bhāvaḥ
This is the intended meaning regarding those absorbed in “I” and “mine.”
entries.literal_english: Samādhi in the Self is steadiness of mind; by the strength of that yoga means. Liberation through the effort of the yoga of knowledge, but through saintly association and hearing Your topics it comes without effort. This is the intended meaning regarding those absorbed in “I” and “mine.”

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं स्तुत्वा प्रार्थयन्ते चतुर्भिः । तत् तस्मात् हे आद्य, ते त्वदीया वयं यस्माल् लोकानां सिसृक्षया त्वयानुसृष्टाः क्रमेणोत्पादिताः । त्रिभिर् आत्मभिः सत्त्वादि-स्वभावैः, अत एव विरुद्ध-स्वभावत्वाद् वियुक्ताः सन्तो यद्-अर्थं सृष्टाः, तत् स्व-विहार-तन्त्रं त्वत्-क्रीडोपकरणं ब्रह्माण्डं, ते तुभ्यं प्रतिहर्तवे प्रतिहर्तुं समर्पयितुं न शक्नुमः, अतस् त्वं नः स्व-चक्षुः परिदेहीति त्रयाणां श्लोकानां चतुर्थेनान्वयः ॥४७॥
word_for_word: tad evaṃ stutvā prārthayante caturbhiḥ
Having thus praised Him, they pray in four verses.
tat tasmāt he ādya, te tvadīyā vayaṃ yasmāl lokānāṃ sisṛkṣayā tvayānusṛṣṭāḥ krameṇotpāditāḥ
Therefore, O First One, we are Yours, since You created us in sequence out of the desire to create the worlds.

tribhir ātmabhiḥ sattvādi-svabhāvaiḥ, ata eva viruddha-svabhāvatvād viyuktāḥ santo yad-arthaṃ sṛṣṭāḥ, tat sva-vihāra-tantraṃ tvat-krīḍopakaraṇaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ, te tubhyaṃ pratihartave pratihartuṃ samarpayituṃ na śaknumaḥ, atas tvaṃ naḥ sva-cakṣuḥ paridehīti trayāṇāṃ ślokānāṃ caturthenānvayaḥ

Separated through the three selves, the natures beginning with sattva, and therefore opposed in nature, we cannot return to You the universe, created as the instrument of Your play, for whose purpose we were created; therefore the fourth verse is connected with the request, “grant us Your own vision.”

entries.sanskrit: असामर्थ्यम् एव प्रपञ्चयितुं कार्यस्यातिवैचित्र्यम् आहुः । भो अज ! काले तत्-तद्-अवसरे बलिं भोगं यावत् साकल्येन ते तुभ्यं हराम समर्पयाम । यथा येन प्रकारेणान्नम् अदाम भक्षयामेत्य् अनेनान्न-मात्रं चास्माकम्, ऐश्वर्येण तु भोगस् तवैवेत्य् उक्तम् । उभयेषां तव चास्माकं च यत्र स्थित्वा इमे जीवा अनूहा अप्रत्यूहा निर्विघ्नाः । यद् वा, अनूहा अवितर्काः, निःसंशया इत्य् अर्थः । तथा च श्रुतिः---ता एनम् अब्रुवन्न् आयतनं नः प्रजानीहि यस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठिता अन्नम् अदाम् इति ॥४८॥
word_for_word: asāmarthyam eva prapañcayituṃ kāryasyātivaicitryam āhuḥ
To elaborate their inability, they explain the extraordinary variety of the work.
bho aja ! kāle tat-tad-avasare baliṃ bhogaṃ yāvat sākalyena te tubhyaṃ harāma samarpayāma
O Unborn One, at each proper time we shall offer You all food and enjoyment, presenting it completely to You.
yathā yena prakāreṇānnam adāma bhakṣayāmety anenānna-mātraṃ cāsmākam, aiśvaryeṇa tu bhogas tavaivety uktam
We shall eat food in the way ordained; by this it is said that the food is ours, while enjoyment by opulence belongs to You.
ubhayeṣāṃ tava cāsmākaṃ ca yatra sthitvā ime jīvā anūhā apratyūhā nirvighnāḥ
In the place where these living beings exist, for both You and us, they are unhindered and without obstruction.
yad vā, anūhā avitarkāḥ, niḥsaṃśayā ity arthaḥ
Or anūhā means unconsidered, undoubted.
tathā ca śrutiḥ---tā enam abruvann āyatanaṃ naḥ prajānīhi yasmin pratiṣṭhitā annam adām iti
Thus the śruti says: “They said to Him, tell us the abode in which we shall stand and eat food.”

O Unborn One, at each proper time we shall offer You all food and enjoyment, presenting it completely to You. We shall eat food in the way ordained; by this it is said that the food is ours, while enjoyment by opulence belongs to You. In the place where these living beings exist, for both You and us, they are unhindered and without obstruction. Or anūhā means unconsidered, undoubted. Thus the śruti says: “They said to Him, tell us the abode in which we shall stand and eat food.”

entries.sanskrit: अवश्यं च त्वयाऽस्माकम् एषां च कार्योपाधीनां जीवानां वृत्तिः परिकल्पनीया जनकत्वाद् इत्य् आहुः । नोऽस्माकं सान्वयणां स-कार्याणाम् । यद् वा, अन्वेतीत्य् अन्वयः । कारणं तत्-सहितानां त्वम् एवाद्यः कारणम् । अत्र हेतवः---कूट-स्थोऽविक्रियः, पुरुषोऽधिष्ठाता, पुराणः पुरातनः । एतद् उपपादयन्ति---त्वम् इति । हे देव ! अज एव त्वं गुणानां सात्त्वादीनां कर्मणां जन्मादीनां च योनौ कारण-भूतायां शक्त्यां मायायां प्रथमं रेत आदधे । निहितवान् असीत्य् अर्थः । कीदृशं ? कविं सर्व-ज्ञं महत्-तत्त्व-रूपम् ॥४९॥
word_for_word: avaśyaṃ ca tvayā’smākam eṣāṃ ca kāryopādhīnāṃ jīvānāṃ vṛttiḥ parikalpanīyā janakatvād ity āhuḥ
Because You are the creator, You must arrange the livelihood of us and of these living beings defined by their functions.
no’smākaṃ sānvayaṇāṃ sa-kāryāṇām
Not only for us, together with our successors and functions.
yad vā, anvetīty anvayaḥ
Or anvaya means that which follows.
kāraṇaṃ tat-sahitānāṃ tvam evādyaḥ kāraṇam
You alone are the original cause of those together with their functions.
atra hetavaḥ---kūṭa-stho’vikriyaḥ, puruṣo’dhiṣṭhātā, purāṇaḥ purātanaḥ
The reasons are: You are unchanging, the Person, the overseer, ancient and primeval.
etad upapādayanti---tvam iti
They establish this with the word “You.”
he deva ! aja eva tvaṃ guṇānāṃ sāttvādīnāṃ karmaṇāṃ janmādīnāṃ ca yonau kāraṇa-bhūtāyāṃ śaktyāṃ māyāyāṃ prathamaṃ reta ādadhe
O Lord, unborn as You are, You first placed the seed in māyā, the power that is the cause of the guṇas, actions and births.
nihitavān asīty arthaḥ
That is, You placed it there.
kīdṛśaṃ ? kaviṃ sarva-jñaṃ mahat-tattva-rūpam
What kind? Omniscient, in the form of mahat-tattva.
entries.literal_english: Because You are the creator, You must arrange the livelihood of us and of these living beings defined by their functions. Not only for us, together with our successors and functions. Or anvaya means that which follows. You alone are the original cause of those together with their functions. The reasons are: You are unchanging, the Person, the overseer, ancient and primeval. They establish this with the word “You.” O Lord, unborn as You are, You first placed the seed in māyā, the power that is the cause of the guṇas, actions and births. That is, You placed it there. What kind? Omniscient, in the form of mahat-tattva.

entries.sanskrit: तथा हे आत्मन् देव ! सत्-प्रमुखा महद्-आदयो वयं यद्-अर्थं बभूविम, तत् किं ते कार्यं करवाम ? सृष्टिम् इति चेत् तत्राहुः । तर्हि नोऽस्माकं त्वं स्व-चक्षुः स्वीयं ज्ञानं शक्त्या सह परिदेहि प्रयच्छ । यस्मात् त्वत्त एवानुग्रहो येषां ते यद्-अनुग्रहास् तेषाम् अस्माकम् । क्रियार्थे इयान् एवैतावान् अनुग्रहो येषाम् इत्य् एकं वा पदम् । त्वदीय-ज्ञान-क्रिया-शक्तिभ्याम् एव वयं सृष्टौ क्षमा नान्यथेत्य् अर्थः ॥५०॥
word_for_word: tathā he ātman deva ! sat-pramukhā mahad-ādayo vayaṃ yad-arthaṃ babhūvima, tat kiṃ te kāryaṃ karavāma ? sṛṣṭim iti cet tatrāhuḥ
Likewise, O Self, O Lord, we—beginning with sattva and the mahat principle—have come into being for some purpose; what service shall we perform for You? If the answer is “creation,” they say this.
tarhi no’smākaṃ tvaṃ sva-cakṣuḥ svīyaṃ jñānaṃ śaktyā saha paridehi prayaccha
Then grant us Your own vision, Your knowledge, together with potency.
yasmāt tvatta evānugraho yeṣāṃ te yad-anugrahās teṣām asmākam
Since those who receive grace from You are the objects of Your favor, we are among them.
kriyārthe iyān evaitāvān anugraho yeṣām ity ekaṃ vā padam
Or this may be one compound: their grace is just this much.
tvadīya-jñāna-kriyā-śaktibhyām eva vayaṃ sṛṣṭau kṣamā nānyathety arthaḥ
We are capable of creation only through Your knowledge and action potencies, and not otherwise.
